newsitem.title: ROMANIA: New Romania PM ponders privatisation ministry.
newsitem.headline: New Romania PM ponders privatisation ministry.

text.p: Romania's Prime Minister- designate Victor Ciorbea said he was considering a merger of two institutions to create a new privatisation ministry in his reformist goverment.

In an interview late on Wednesay, he said he would consider merging the Economic Reform Council, which oversees market reforms, and the State Ownership Fund (FPS), which retains a controlling interest in 5,000 state firms.
"We have not yet taken a final decision," he said. "We'll see. Our stand on this will be clarified within 10 days."

President-elect Emil Constantinescu, who ousted ex-communists in last weekend's election, and his Democratic Convention centrist bloc have called for faster reforms, a revamp of privatisation and restructuring of industry.
Romania embarked on a privatisation scheme in 1991, two years after the fall of communism, with plans to turn 6,500 firms over to the private sector.
Analysts have said the process would have been more effective with streamlined bodies within a single ministry.

The FPS initially held 70 percent of the companies earmarked for privatisation, with the remaining 30 percent in the hands of five regional private ownership funds (FPPs). From November, these have been turned into U.S.-style mutual funds.

Last year, the outgoing leftist government launched a mass sell-off, offering Romanians stakes of up to 60 percent in 4,000 of the companies in exchange for privatisation coupons and vouchers. The remainder was to be sold off for cash.

Analysts say the sell-off against privatisation paper has proved a success but that cash sales should proceed more quickly to attract capital needed for reforms. -- Ron Popeski, Bucharest newsroom +401 312-0264
